competing_explanations: Natural-language messages contain no complete proposals, so a majority/always-negative baseline performs as well as the Monitor.
The Monitor prediction changes reflect schema/order bias or provider variation rather than message semantics.
Human coders cannot reliably distinguish proposal, acceptance, and ambiguity under the task codebook.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: Freeze all 96 chat message slots, including no_message, and use two independent human coders plus adjudication before any Monitor call. Run frozen proposal and recipient-action-concordance tasks, plus 12 paired capability controls. A failure of coder agreement, positive controls, or Monitor improvement over the literal baseline falsifies the proposed LLM-specific value claim.
candidates.hypothesis: On the prospective M1 message slots, a privileged-evidence Monitor will recover complete allocation proposals and recipient-ballot concordance against independently double-coded human references better than a literal mapping baseline, while preserving abstentions and citation validity.
candidates.selection_note: Supporting Track 2.2 candidate only. Defer until blinded human codebook/adjudication is available. It cannot create a latent-collusion label; structured public harm remains a deterministic rule output.
candidates.title: Can a Monitor extract proposal and ballot-concordance facts from natural-language messages?

competing_explanations: The common +20 HH incentive independently produces the same choices with or without peer delivery; parallel behavior is not communication-induced coordination.
The finite differences reflect one deterministic call order, scenario/proposer assignment, or provider state rather than message delivery.
Actual and neutral message prompts differ in semantic content, length, wording, and salience; the resulting contrast is not a pure semantic effect.
Both roles are stateless contexts of the same model alias; behavior does not generalize to independent models or persistent agents.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: For each of three fixed matrices, compare one actual-delivery arm with one no-delivery arm. A positive finite-set pattern requires all three pairs to be assessable and actual delivery to produce HH while no-delivery does not in at least two pairs. The neutral-substitution arm is a secondary comparator. Any outcome is descriptive for this fixed model/API run, with no p-values, population inference, latent collusion label, or claim that agreement proves communication-caused coordination.
candidates.hypothesis: Across three preregistered two-agent payoff matrices, the actual-message-delivery policy will produce joint HIGH in at least two matrices where the matched no-delivery policy does not.
candidates.selection_note: Selected for a bounded, user-approved three-matrix pilot after the prior Recipient V1 fact-control failure and downstream truncation defect. It studies observable message routing and ballots only. The common target incentive and three fixed contexts make this a descriptive falsification pilot, not a collusion test.
candidates.title: Does peer-message routing change joint choices under a shared incentive in three fixed games?

policy: At most three read-only candidate directions may be compared. Only one can be selected for a formal cycle at a time. Candidate status is not preregistration or authorization.
